## TL;DR

The review (pass 8, "needs some work") named five bug classes in the close-out progress feature. This round fixes them in the recorder, the job coordinator, the remote runner and the pipeline label, and adds the attempt-renewal path so a retry gets its own attempt and log. The drawer shot now declares step, host and attempt. The local scoped check is green. The remote gate stopped on a WebKit perf budget once and then on a missing report draft, which this file fixes.

## Work and rationale

- **Heartbeats emit a snapshot.** `CloseOutProgressRecorder` now calls `onChange` after every persisted write, heartbeats included. The card and drawer see a live `lastProgressAt` during a quiet sync or publish instead of a false stall.
- **Failed writes are retried, not dropped.** A log line or job-record write that does not land is kept and sent with the next write. `lastProgressAt` moves only when the log line landed, so a dead log can no longer look fresh. Pending lines are capped at 100.
- **Staleness is judged on the recorder alone.** `buildIntegrationSnapshot` checks `progressIsStale` against the attempt's own timestamp. Fresh stage events still show as the "last seen" time, but they no longer mask a recorder that stopped writing.
- **Host-slot wait is visible.** The Tailscale pool loop reports `queued` from `onQueue` and `acquired` with the host once it holds a slot. The orchestrator maps these to "queued for host slot" (no host) and "remote validation" (with host). Before this, a run waiting for a slot was not registered and the close-out could not show the wait.
- **Remote build is not labelled as tests.** The combined `run` stage now maps to "remote validation". `ActiveRemoteRunRegistry.setTestProgress` moves the run to `test` on its first test marker, so build and test phases are timed separately.
- **Retries are new attempts.** `advanceAttempt` in the job coordinator writes a new generation, sets `previousFailure` to the failure that caused it, and clears step, host and progress. The recorder's `beginAttempt` moves the log to the new attempt and records the reason on both logs. Gate reruns and host failover both use this path. A cancelled record is never advanced.
- **Stalled labels keep context.** The stalled label names the step it stopped on and the retry reason, for both card and drawer.
- **Fixture.** `drawer:closeOutRemoteTests` carries step "running tests (27/84)", host "bee", attempt 2, and a previous failure.

## Approaches tried

I first planned a separate `renewAttempt` coordinator method. The committed work already had `advanceAttempt` on the same record with the same fencing, so I kept it instead of adding a second method. I also considered judging staleness from the newest of the stage events and recorder writes. That is what the review flagged, so staleness now uses the recorder only.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Worktree lock.** While each handoff check ran, RepoOS made the `src/` files read-only. Edits failed until the check finished. I did not override the lock. The first handoff failed because my uncommitted edits changed the tree mid-check.
- **Concurrent checkpoints.** Several WIP checkpoint commits in this worktree (08:44–08:59) came from an earlier engineer turn that is no longer live. I verified them against the review findings and built on them rather than rewriting them.
- **Server timeouts.** A handoff ran for roughly 15 minutes and then failed with "server-side finalization timed out". I cannot fix that from the branch.
- **Perf budget on the remote runner.** The WebKit work-board test at 375px on bee failed its timing budget. The same test passes locally (3/3 in 38 seconds). The work board code is not in this change, so I read it as runner load. I did not loosen the budget.
- **Missing report draft.** The handoff stopped at review because `.repoos/engineering-report-drafts/1276.md` did not exist in the worktree. This file is that draft, and it is rewritten here after the earlier copy disappeared.

## Key learnings

- A handoff request made from a linked worktree is only finalized when the turn ends. A request that is not followed by ending the turn does not reach the server.
- Edits during a running check are unsafe even when the check does not read them. The lock exists for that reason.
- For a timing-sensitive browser test, a loaded runner can fail where the same test passes on an idle machine. Check whether the failing test covers the changed code before treating the failure as real. Here it does not.
